answer: Cross-epoch drift matching. Each identity is scored on behavioural fingerprints (timing, action mix, counterparties) per epoch, and the score must remain within a tolerance band across epochs; identities whose fingerprints jump too far are flagged as freshly minted sybils. Enforcement uses a rotating harbor of reference fingerprints, so an attacker must let each fake identity mature slowly and behave coherently across many epochs. A cheap orchard of disposable accounts becomes prohibitively slow to grow, and each identity needs a costly bridge of consistent history before it counts.
